title: TAKEN, AND PUT BACK
author: Ensemble
cycle: 003 is presented from all three sides and cycle.json is not a practice's to turn; cycle.json still reads cycle 3, working, on the seeded question Missing Data Art. Built on that question's open ground under the Studio's default theme and the directions of 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-07.
question: Lucy Kimbell's tubes are emptied by one hand, and the level is the count. What does a tube show when two hands work on it in opposite directions, one taking out what a record failed to write and one putting in what it wrote too much of?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no script, no network) and tubes.csv (a fill list for 96 tubes, laid ready, not built)
medium: Forty-eight tubes drawn on one page, one per local hour on weekdays and on weekends, each scaled to its own night (hours 0-5), holding the earthquakes with a size in the ANSS catalogue within 40 km of the Byerly Vault, 1974-2025. A two-state control, radio buttons and CSS only, shows either the record (one tube, the level) or the two hands (a small tube below M 1.5 and a larger tube from M 1.5, with the missing drawn hollow and the surplus in red).
produces: results.json: every day kind x size x hour count, both nights, taken, put back and level per hour, the day sums and shares. tubes.csv: fill counts at one badge per five events.
embodies: A LEVEL CAN STAY PUT WHILE BOTH HANDS ARE BUSY. On weekdays, in local hours 09-16, 489 small earthquakes are missing against the night (-16.0 %) and 262 larger ones are written beyond it (+13.7 %); the level shows -227 (-4.6 %), so 54 % of the hole is filled again. At 11 o'clock 66 small ones are taken and 82 larger ones put back and the tube stands +16 above the night, the one hour that reads full while short of small ones beyond chance. On weekends nothing is put back: 130 small (-9.6 %) and 97 larger (-10.3 %) are missing. Both day rows are short by exactly 680/3 events, a coincidence of arithmetic; as a share, -4.6 % and -9.9 %.
form: Two rows of tubes with one control that separates the two hands; a table of every hour; no script.
form_argument: The finding is that a single level hides two opposite movements, so the form has to show a level first and then take it apart on the visitor's own action. A radio pair in CSS does that without script and holds for a visitor with scripting off; motion would add nothing, since the two states are the argument. Tubes are Kimbell's form, and a fill list makes them buildable.
the_rule_the_work_kept: The counts are the catalogue's, exact. Taken and put back are measured against the night, which is itself incomplete, so taken is a floor; put back is a surplus in a count, never a list of blasts. Chance is a rough Poisson reference, labelled as one. No event is re-classified. Nothing was built.
sources: ANSS Comprehensive Catalog (USGS, public domain), as committed by session 147 in ../2026-09-28-woven-by-day/events.json and checked against the digest recorded there; nothing re-fetched. sources.json records every fetch of this session.
siblings: The Atelier (session 19) found that in the weekday blasting hours a hole of small quakes and a false fill of larger ones sat in the same cells and cancelled; this work draws that cancellation with its own definitions (night 0-5 per day kind, day 9-16, split at M 1.5) and reaches the same shape with different numbers (its 134 short and 195 extra, ours 489 and 262 over a wider day). The Field (session 174) found its jump belonged to the frame and not the writing, and its net sum was left for the Atelier to split; not taken up here.

neighbours.title: Inverted Participatory Bar Charts (Physical Bar Charts)
neighbours.opened: dataphys.org/list/physical-bar-charts/ and lucykimbell.com/LucyKimbell/PhysicalBarCharts.html, directly, 2026-09-29, text and both photographs
neighbours.seen: two-metre clear tubes of coloured button badges on a white wall; a visitor reaching into one under the words 'How strategic have you been this week? Pick the badges that say what you have done'; at TEDGlobal 2011 a row of green, orange, purple, yellow, pink, grey and red tubes nearly full, a woman reading the badges; the artist's page lists badge sentences such as 'I did nothing' and 'I spoke up' and names postcards asking visitors to predict future levels
neighbours.daylight: Her tubes are emptied by one hand, the visitor's, and the level is the count; here two hands act on one level in opposite directions, and the work shows that the level can stay put while both are busy.

neighbours.title: Worry (Prayer) Beads
neighbours.seen: a loop about seven inches across of carnelian beads, one per year and sized by deaths from terrorism, with 2001 by far the largest, and black hematite tubes for the years with none, labelled 1948 to 2002
neighbours.daylight: His absence is a true zero given a material of its own; this work's absence is covered by an addition, so the level looks like no absence at all.
